sources.title: Sample source pack: skill statements by Security+ domain (stand-in until the published SY0-801 objectives are loaded at Discovery)
sources.text:
Domain 1.
Security Controls: Classify a security control by category (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and type (preventive, detective, corrective, deterrent, compensating, directive).
Information Security: Explain how confidentiality, integrity, availability, AAA and non-repudiation apply to a workplace system.
Wireshark: Identify protocols, ports and the TCP handshake in a packet capture using Wireshark display filters.
Zero Trust: Describe how zero trust uses policy decision and enforcement points to replace implicit trust.
Multi-Factor Authentication: Select an MFA method for a use case, including phishing-resistant options, and justify it against NIST SP 800-63B-4.
Hashing: Use hashing to verify file integrity and explain why salting defeats precomputed attacks.
Public Key Infrastructure: Generate a key pair and certificate signing request, and inspect a TLS certificate chain.
Domain 2.
Threat Intelligence: Compare threat actors by motive, resources and capability.
Malware Analysis: Identify malware, password, application and network attacks from their indicators.
Phishing: Analyze a suspicious email's headers and SPF, DKIM and DMARC results to decide whether it is phishing.
MITRE ATT&CK Framework: Map an observed attack behavior to a MITRE ATT&CK technique with supporting evidence.
AI Security: Explain AI-enabled attacks (deepfake voice, AI-written phishing) and attacks on AI assistants (prompt injection), and the controls that counter them.
Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS): Prioritize vulnerabilities using CVSS v4.0, CISA KEV status and asset criticality.
OWASP: Recognize common application weaknesses from the OWASP Top 10.
Domain 3.
Subnetting: Calculate IPv4 subnets and spot hosts outside an expected range.
Active Directory: Configure role-based groups and least-privilege permissions in Active Directory, removing standing admin rights.
Firewall: Write firewall rules that segment user, server and guest networks by least privilege, and prove them with test traffic.
Cloud Security: Distinguish customer and provider security responsibilities under IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.
System Hardening: Harden a Linux server against a CIS Benchmark and document an accepted exception.
Cloud Infrastructure Security: Identify cloud misconfigurations such as public storage and over-broad roles.
Endpoint Detection And Response: Explain how endpoint detection and response, backups and high availability support resilience.
Domain 4.
Identity And Access Management (IAM): Apply account lifecycle controls (provisioning, access review, offboarding) to prevent orphaned access.
Vulnerability Scanning: Run discovery and vulnerability scans against authorized hosts with Nmap and Greenbone OpenVAS.
Vulnerability Assessments: Validate scanner findings by hand and remove false positives.
Vulnerability Management: Recommend remediation or a compensating control with an owner, deadline and verification step.
Log Analysis: Identify which log source (Windows event, firewall, DNS, EDR) answers a given investigative question.
Security Information And Event Management (SIEM): Write and tune a SIEM search for a known attack pattern in Splunk or Security Onion.
Alert Triage: Triage an alert to a true or false positive decision using log evidence and threat intelligence enrichment.
Security Operations: Document an alert in a ticket that meets SOC Tier 1 standards, and escalate it by defined criteria.
Generative Artificial Intelligence: Check AI-assisted triage output against raw evidence before acting on it.
Incident Response Plan: Apply the NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 incident response model, organized by CSF 2.0 functions, to a live incident.
Incident Response: Choose containment, eradication and recovery actions that balance spread against business impact.
Chain Of Custody: Preserve evidence in order of volatility with chain of custody.
Digital Forensics: Build an incident timeline from Windows event logs and prefetch artifacts.
Technical Writing: Write an incident report with root cause and lessons learned for a leader.
Domain 5.
Security Policies: Distinguish policies, standards, procedures and guidelines, and apply the right one to a situation.
Risk Analysis: Calculate SLE, ARO and ALE, and record a risk with a treatment decision in a risk register.
NIST Cybersecurity Framework: Use a NIST CSF 2.0 profile to rank security improvements for an organization.
Executive Communication: Write a security recommendation a non-technical leader can approve, with risk, cost range and the decision needed.
Acceptable Use Policy: Apply acceptable-use and governance rules to generative AI tools that handle company data.

sources.title: Sample source pack: course learning outcomes (stand-in until UMGC outcomes are loaded at Discovery)
sources.text:
CLO1: Apply core security principles and analyze network traffic to judge what is normal on a workplace network.
CLO2: Analyze artifacts to recognize threat actors, attack techniques and social engineering, including AI-enabled attacks, and map them to ATT&CK.
CLO3: Configure least-privilege access, select MFA and apply cryptographic protections to a workplace system.
CLO4: Find, validate, prioritize and track remediation of vulnerabilities on authorized hosts.
CLO5: Design segmented networks and harden systems against published benchmarks.
CLO6: Monitor events in a SIEM, triage alerts to a true or false positive decision and document the decision in a ticket.
CLO7: Run the incident response lifecycle and preserve evidence with chain of custody.
CLO8: Apply risk and governance tools and explain security decisions to non-technical leaders.

competencies.performance_criteria: Maps a real artifact (email, log) to an ATT&CK technique with evidence

competencies.performance_criteria: Builds role-based access with no standing admin rights; verifies integrity and certificates

competencies.name: Vulnerability management
competencies.definition: Finds, validates, prioritizes and tracks remediation of vulnerabilities
competencies.performance_criteria: Removes false positives; ranks by CVSS, KEV and asset value; sets owner and deadline

competencies.name: Secure architecture and hardening
competencies.definition: Designs segmented networks and hardens systems against benchmarks
competencies.performance_criteria: Writes firewall rules that enforce least privilege; fixes benchmark findings and documents exceptions

competencies.name: Security monitoring and alert triage
competencies.definition: Monitors events in a SIEM, triages alerts and documents decisions
competencies.performance_criteria: Reaches the right true or false positive call with log evidence; writes a ticket another analyst can act on

competencies.name: Incident response and evidence handling
competencies.definition: Runs the incident response lifecycle and preserves evidence
competencies.performance_criteria: Builds an evidence-based timeline; chooses safe containment; keeps chain of custody
competencies.evidence: Forensics lab, Incident Response Report, capstone

competencies.name: Governance, risk and communication
competencies.definition: Applies risk and governance tools and explains security to non-technical leaders
competencies.performance_criteria: Builds a risk register entry with ALE; writes a ranked recommendation a leader can approve
